title: Numbers & Algebra
source: Sullivan 10e; Aufmann, Barker & Nation 7e; additions from Axler and Stewart

children.title: Why do we keep inventing new kinds of number?
children.summary: Climbs a tower N → Z → Q → R → C; each level exists to solve an equation the one below can't (x + 5 = 2, 2x = 3, x² = 2, x² = −1)

children.title: Why is √2 not a fraction?
children.summary: Zooms a grid of fractions p/q toward √2 and never lands; then steps through the 'both even' contradiction proof

children.title: Why do repeating decimals always come from fractions?
children.summary: Runs long division of p/q: only q possible remainders, so one must repeat; also watches the gap between 0.999… and 1 shrink to nothing

children.title: Why is (−) × (−) = (+)?
children.summary: Multiplies on a number line where × (−1) is a half-turn; two half-turns bring you home. Also extends the pattern 3 × (−2), 2 × (−2), …

children.title: Why can't we divide by zero?
children.summary: Slides x toward 0 from both sides in 6 ÷ x and watches the answer blow up in opposite directions; asks 'what times 0 gives 6?'

children.title: Why is the order of operations what it is?
children.summary: Evaluates one expression in two orders and gets two answers; the rule is a convention so everyone gets the same one

children.title: Why does (−1)(−1) = 1 follow from the distributive law?
children.summary: Expands (−1)(1 + (−1)) = 0 two ways; the rule is forced, not chosen

children.title: Absolute value is distance
children.summary: Drags a and b on a number line; |a − b| is the gap between them

children.title: Sets and Venn diagrams
children.summary: Builds union, intersection and complement by dragging elements into circles

children.title: Interval notation builder
children.summary: Drags endpoints and toggles open/closed; the notation and the inequality update together

children.title: How Archimedes trapped π
children.summary: Doubles the sides of inscribed and circumscribed polygons and watches the bounds squeeze π

children.title: Why is the empty set a subset of every set?
children.summary: Tries to find an element of ∅ that isn't in A: there is none

children.title: Why does a set of n elements have 2ⁿ subsets?
children.summary: Decides in or out for each element (see Sequences, Counting & Probability → Counting)

children.title: Why is n(A ∪ B) = n(A) + n(B) − n(A ∩ B)?
children.summary: Counts a Venn diagram and sees the overlap counted twice

children.title: Why De Morgan's laws?
children.summary: Shades (A ∪ B)′ and A′ ∩ B′ and finds them identical

children.title: Why three separate tests: reflexive, symmetric, transitive?
children.summary: Toggles arrows on a dot diagram and finds relations that pass any two tests but fail the third (≤ is not symmetric; 'is a sibling of' is not reflexive)

children.title: Roster ↔ set-builder
children.summary: Converts between the two notations

children.title: Intervals as subsets of ℝ
children.summary: Turns intervals into sets and back

children.title: Test a relation
children.summary: Checks a relation on {1, 2, 3} for each property, then adds the fewest pairs needed to make it an equivalence

children.title: Count equivalence relations on {1, 2, 3}
children.summary: Lists the 5 ways to split the set into classes; only 2 of them contain (1, 2)

children.title: Survey problems with Venn diagrams
children.summary: Finds how many like tea only, coffee only or both

children.title: Which day of the week? Classes mod 7
children.summary: Groups dates by remainder mod 7; 'a − b divisible by 7' is an equivalence relation

children.title: Why is a⁰ = 1?
children.summary: Walks down 2³, 2², 2¹ dividing by 2 each step; the pattern forces 2⁰ = 1

children.title: Why is a⁻ⁿ = 1/aⁿ?
children.summary: Keeps halving past zero: 2⁻¹ = ½, 2⁻² = ¼

children.title: Why do exponents add when you multiply?
children.summary: Joins a block of 3 factors to a block of 4 and counts 7

children.title: Why is a^(1/2) = √a?
children.summary: Sees that the exponent laws force (a^½)² = a, so a^½ must be √a; then extends to a^(m/n)

children.title: Why is √(a²) = |a|, not a?
children.summary: Plots y = √(x²) and y = x together; they disagree for every negative x

children.title: Why rationalise the denominator?
children.summary: Divides 1 by 1.41421 by hand versus 1.41421 by 2 and compares the effort; today it's mostly a convention for comparing answers

children.title: Simplify radicals with a factor tree
children.summary: Splits the radicand into prime factors and pulls out pairs

children.title: Scientific notation zoom
children.summary: Slides a power-of-ten dial from nanoseconds to a googol; the mantissa stays between 1 and 10

children.title: Powers of ten: atom to universe
children.summary: Zooms through sizes, each step × 10, and places familiar objects on the scale

children.title: Why is (a + b)² not a² + b²?
children.summary: Builds a square of side a + b and finds the two a × b rectangles everyone forgets

children.title: Why does a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b)?
children.summary: Cuts the L-shape left after removing b² from a² and rearranges it into a rectangle

children.title: Why do a³ ± b³ factor?
children.summary: Splits a cube with a smaller cube removed into three slabs that share the factor (a − b)

children.title: Why does factoring find the solutions?
children.summary: Shrinks one side of a rectangle to zero: a product is 0 only when a factor is 0

children.title: Why does completing the square work?
children.summary: Arranges algebra tiles for x² + bx and sees the missing (b/2)² corner

children.title: Why does synthetic division work?
children.summary: Runs polynomial long division beside synthetic division and watches the x's and repeated numbers drop out

children.title: Algebra tiles: multiply and factor
children.summary: Arranges tiles into a rectangle to factor x² + bx + c and ax² + bx + c

children.title: Polynomial long division
children.summary: Divides step by step beside a matching numeric long division

children.title: Factor by grouping
children.summary: Groups terms and pulls out the common binomial

children.title: Why can't you cancel the x in (x + 2)/x?
children.summary: Plugs in numbers and sees that you can cancel factors, never terms

children.title: Why do we need a common denominator?
children.summary: Adds fraction bars of different sizes; they only combine once cut into equal pieces, and the same holds for algebra

children.title: Why does a 'simplified' expression hide a hole?
children.summary: Graphs (x² − 1)/(x − 1) and x + 1; they match everywhere except x = 1

children.title: LCM method for rational expressions
children.summary: Factors denominators, builds the LCM, then adds

children.title: Simplify complex fractions
children.summary: Multiplies top and bottom by the LCM and watches the layers collapse

children.title: Two pipes fill a tank
children.summary: Combines rates 1/a + 1/b and finds the joint time

children.title: Why invent i at all?
children.summary: Follows Cardano's formula on x³ = 15x + 4: it needs √−121 on the way to the real root 4 (Bombelli's insight)

children.title: Why multiply by the conjugate to divide?
children.summary: Sees (a + bi)(a − bi) = a² + b², a real number, and the conjugate as a mirror image on the plane

children.title: Why do complex roots come in conjugate pairs?
children.summary: Lifts a parabola above the axis; its roots appear as a ± bi mirror images

children.title: Why do the powers of i cycle?
children.summary: Multiplies by i repeatedly: i, −1, −i, 1, a quarter-turn each time (see Trigonometry → Polar & Complex)

children.title: Why can't we say one complex number is bigger than another?
children.summary: Tries to order i and 0 and hits a contradiction either way

children.title: Complex arithmetic on the plane
children.summary: Adds and multiplies by dragging points; the sum is vector addition

children.title: Solve quadratics in the complex numbers
children.summary: Sees a negative discriminant give two conjugate roots

children.title: Modulus and argument on the Argand plane
children.summary: Reads r and θ off the plane

children.title: Why do the same thing to both sides?
children.summary: Keeps a balance level while removing equal weights; al-jabr means 'restoration'

children.title: Why can an equation have no solution, or every solution?
children.summary: Graphs both sides as lines: crossing, parallel or identical

children.title: Why can clearing fractions create fake solutions?
children.summary: Multiplies by an expression that can be 0 and checks which answers survive

children.title: Rearrange any formula
children.summary: Picks a variable in a formula (v = u + at, A = P(1 + rt)) and isolates it step by step

children.title: Why does a mixture land between its ingredients?
children.summary: Mixes two strengths on a lever; the result is the weighted average

children.title: Uniform motion on a distance–time graph
children.summary: Runs two trains; the crossing point solves the equation

children.title: Simple interest and job-rate problems
children.summary: Sets up and solves the classic word problems with a diagram first

children.title: Why the quadratic formula?
children.summary: Completes the square on ax² + bx + c with algebra tiles, one tile move per algebra line (spec below)
children.spec: Tiles: ax² + bx + c laid out as tiles; divide by a, and each algebra line appears beside the tile move that makes it. Missing corner: the x² square plus two (b/2a)x strips leaves a gap of exactly (b/2a)², which you add to both sides. Square root: the completed square gives (x + b/2a)² = (b² − 4ac)/4a², and the ± appears because both sides of the square count. Check: sliders for a, b and c, with roots marked on a live parabola so the formula's answer visibly lands on the axis crossings.

children.title: Why does the discriminant count the roots?
children.summary: Slides a parabola up and down: it crosses the axis 2, 1 or 0 times as b² − 4ac changes sign

children.title: Why are the sum and product of roots −b/a and c/a?
children.summary: Expands a(x − r)(x − s) and matches coefficients live

children.title: Why do radical equations give extraneous roots?
children.summary: Squares both sides and sees the graphs of y = √x and y = −√x merge into one parabola

children.title: Choose a method: factor, complete, or formula
children.summary: Gets a quadratic and sees which method is quickest and why

children.title: Equations quadratic in form
children.summary: Substitutes u = x² in x⁴ − 5x² + 4 = 0 and maps the u-roots back to x

children.title: When does the ball land?
children.summary: Throws a ball, reads h(t) = 0 and gets two roots, one of them rejected

children.title: A Babylonian problem solved with geometry
children.summary: Solves a 1800 BC word problem by cutting and moving squares

children.title: Why does multiplying by a negative flip the sign?
children.summary: Multiplies two points by −1 on a number line; their order reverses

children.title: Why is |x| < a an 'and' but |x| > a an 'or'?
children.summary: Sees 'within a of 0' as one band and 'more than a away' as two rays

children.title: Why do sign charts work?
children.summary: Sees a polynomial change sign only at its zeros (or a rational function at its asymptotes) and tests one point per region

children.title: Quadratic inequality = above or below the axis
children.summary: Shades where the parabola is above or below y = 0

children.title: Why is |a + b| ≤ |a| + |b|?
children.summary: Places a and b on a number line: equal when they point the same way, smaller when they cancel (triangle inequality)

children.title: Combined inequalities
children.summary: Solves a < 2x + 1 ≤ b and reads the interval off

children.title: Absolute value equations: two cases
children.summary: Splits |2x − 3| = 5 into its two mirror cases

children.title: Machining tolerance
children.summary: Writes '5.00 ± 0.02 cm' as |x − 5| ≤ 0.02 and checks parts

children.title: Why does direct variation pass through the origin?
children.summary: Scales k and sees every line y = kx pivot about (0, 0)

children.title: Why does inverse variation never touch the axes?
children.summary: Holds xy = k fixed while sliding x; y can shrink but never reach 0

children.title: Why is light inverse-square?
children.summary: Spreads the same light over spheres of area 4πr², so the intensity falls as 1/r²

children.title: Find k, then predict
children.summary: Uses one data point to fix k, then predicts another

children.title: Joint and combined variation
children.summary: Explores Hooke's law, Ohm's law and the gas law as variation
